variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 1NR-FE
variants.intro: The Toyota NR family uses multiple engine codes that share the same physical architecture but differ in displacement, ECU mapping, and emissions equipment. Fitting the wrong revision will trigger ECU faults and potentially fail an MOT emissions test. 1. Engine Bay Sticker: Located on the inner wing or strut tower. The code is printed clearly alongside the chassis number.

relatives.description: The 1NR-FE was developed to replace the older NZ-series engines in compact applications. While the NZ engines are legendary for their durability, the NR family was designed with a lighter aluminium block, Dual VVT-i on both camshafts, and a focus on improved urban fuel economy and lower emissions. They are not interchangeable.

In later production years, Toyota updated the 1NR-FE to the 1NR-FKE. The core block remains identical, but the FKE variant features VVT-iE (Electric Variable Valve Timing-intelligent) on the intake camshaft for finer control. While physically similar, the ECU and wiring loom differences mean an FKE unit is not a plug-and-play swap for an older FE unit without significant modification.

Sharing the exact same NR family architecture, the 2NR-FE features a larger 1,496cc displacement, a different intake manifold, and distinct ECU calibration to produce higher torque. Attempting to install a 2NR-FE into a 1NR-FE chassis will result in persistent check engine lights, incorrect fueling, and a failed MOT emissions test.

While the 1NR-FE is predominantly badged as a Toyota in the UK (Yaris, Auris, iQ), the broader NR architecture underpins several Daihatsu models. However, UK replacement buyers should always source a unit explicitly coded as 1NR-FE to ensure compatibility with UK-specific emissions mapping and ancillary bracket orientations.

The older predecessor. Physically larger and uses a different engine mount configuration. Not a direct swap. 2NR-FE: 1.5L Dual VVT-i. Shares the exact same NR block architecture as the 1NR-FE, but features a larger displacement, different intake manifold, and distinct ECU calibration. If you are sourcing a replacement 1NR-FE engine, ensure the supplier guarantees the exact code. A 2NR-FE unit will physically bolt into the same chassis mounts, but the ECU, exhaust routing, and intake plumbing will not match without significant modification.

buyingGuide.title: Toyota 1NR-FE Buying Guide

options.label: Used
options.body: A used 1NR-FE engine (£300-£700 ) is a viable option if the donor vehicle has low mileage and a documented service history proving regular oil changes. However, without a warranty on the piston rings and VVT-i system, you inherit the same failure risks. Explore used Toyota engines .

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: The reconditioned 1NR-FE (£900-£1,800 ) is the most popular choice. A proper reconditioning process replaces the piston rings with updated designs, validates the VVT-i gears, and installs a new timing chain and tensioner. This addresses the engine's primary weak points and offers the best balance of cost and reliability. Compare reconditioned Toyota engines .

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A rebuilt 1NR-FE (£1,500-£2,800 ) involves stripping the block to bare metal, machining the cylinder head and block, and replacing all internal bearings and seals. This is only recommended if the original 1NR-FE suffered catastrophic failure (e.g., timing chain snap causing valve damage). View rebuilt Toyota engines .

items.question: How much does a reconditioned Toyota 1NR-FE 1.33L engine cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Toyota 1NR-FE engine typically costs between £900 and £1,800 for supply-only . This price band reflects a unit that has had the documented weak points (specifically the piston ring design and VVT-i components) addressed with updated parts, offering the best balance of reliability and value for this specific code.

items.question: What are the most common failures of the Toyota 1NR-FE engine?
items.answer: The two most documented failure patterns for the 1NR-FE are excessive oil consumption due to the original piston ring design (typically appearing between 60k-100k miles) and VVT-i gear rattle or timing chain stretch on cold startup (80k-120k miles). If oil consumption is ignored, it can lead to catastrophic oil starvation and scored cylinder bores, necessitating a full Toyota 1NR-FE engine replacement.

items.question: Can I fit a 2NR-FE or 1NR-FKE engine in place of my failed 1NR-FE?
items.answer: Physically, the blocks share the same mounting points. However, the 2NR-FE has a different displacement and intake setup, while the 1NR-FKE uses an electric VVT-i actuator. Fitting either without swapping the corresponding ECU, wiring loom, and intake components will result in persistent fault codes, poor drivability, and an MOT failure. Always source an exact-code 1NR-FE replacement.

items.question: How long does it take to replace a Toyota 1NR-FE engine?
items.answer: Independent UK specialists typically quote 6 to 8 hours of labour for a Toyota 1NR-FE engine removal and refit (R&R). This translates to a typical fitted labour premium of £390 to £520 , depending on regional labour rates and whether ancillary components (like the alternator or AC compressor) are transferred or replaced.

items.question: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Toyota Yaris or Auris with a 1NR-FE code?
items.answer: In most cases, yes. The typical UK market value for a 1NR-FE-equipped Toyota Yaris or Auris ranges from £1,500 to £8,000 . A reconditioned Toyota 1NR-FE engine replacement cost is generally viable. However, this carries a ⚠️ Watch flag: if your specific vehicle is at the very bottom of this value range (e.g., an older, high-mileage example valued under £3,000), the replacement cost may approach 60% of the vehicle's value. In such cases, evaluate scrap or part-exchange value before committing to the repair.
